title: What is Strategic Threat Intelligence? | Recorded Future
content_md: Key Takeaways Threat intelligence is often thought of as a single function, but in reality, it can be broken down into four categories: strategic, tactical, operational, and technical. Strategic threat intelligence is non-technical and is used by high-level strategists to inform specific decisions. For the most part, strategic threat intelligence comes from freely available sources. However, the volume of available sources, combined with language constraints, often makes manual collection infeasible. The success of strategic threat intelligence depends on strong two-way communication between threat analysts and their primary audience — usually the board of directors. On the surface, threat intelligence appears to be a single discipline, closely intertwined with the cyber threat intelligence cycle . Practitioners collect data from a variety of sources, analyze it, and use the outputs to make decisions. The reality is a little more complicated. As with most specialties, threat intelligence can be broken down into subcategories, each with its own uses, techniques, and challenges.
